clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8048 is its operative paragraph, which exempts John G. Crane from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending February 29, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting John G. Crane, who, during the current month, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on February 29, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later event is recorded for this clause: no held order text revokes, amends, extends or otherwise cites this order (see the earlier-end check).

research_rationale:
EO 8048 (February 14, 1939) exempts John G. Crane from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending February 29, 1940", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on February 29, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. No later instrument affecting this order was found in the held corpus. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. Re-collation 2026-11-08: the working text was compared word by word with the held GPO printing (jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_8048.txt, page record in PAGE_CHECKS.csv); number, title, date, signature, completeness and every quoted span agree apart from OCR noise (printing header stamps, spaced punctuation, broken hyphens).

savings.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
